chunks: Does he think that no one has power over him?

key_terms.لَنْ: Not ever / Never (particle of negation for the future)

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'he' that thinks no one can overpower him in this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is frequently interpreted as addressing the arrogant elite, particularly the Quraysh leaders or Umayyad caliphs, who relied on worldly power to defy divine authority. It highlights the transient nature of temporal dominance and serves as a warning that no amount of wealth can shield one from the inevitable reckoning of Allah. The rhetorical question underscores the psychological delusion of invincibility that characterizes historical oppressors.
